stem:
Omkar draws rectangle $ABCD$ with diagonal $AC$, as in the diagram.

Which claim about the areas is correct?

options.text: Triangle $ABC$ has half the area of rectangle $ABCD$.
The area of triangle $ABC$ equals the length of diagonal $AC$.
Rectangle $ABCD$ has half the area of triangle $ABC$.
Triangle $ABC$ and rectangle $ABCD$ have the same area.

teacher.key_rationale: A diagonal splits a rectangle into two triangles of equal area, so triangle ABC has half the area of rectangle ABCD. Area is not a length. The rectangle is not half the triangle. Sharing the diagonal does not make the areas equal as wholes.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote kite grid to rectangle ABCD with diagonal AC.
